subject: Backup retention & deletion propagation — LumenPay compliance checklist

To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Wilson <alex.wilson@lumenpay.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Backup retention & deletion propagation — initial questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our data lifecycle plan for payments-related PII and need to confirm how Redwood handles backup retention and deletion propagation across regions. A few concrete questions: 

- If we request deletion of a customer record (legal erase) in the primary region, how and when is that deletion reflected in offsite backups and DR replicas?
- Is there any window where deleted data might exist in immutable snapshots or tape-like offsite copies?
- Can you provide an example timeline from request to full expunge (including tombstone lifecycle) and what audit evidence we'd get?

We have a compliance review next week and would like an answer we can present.

Appreciate any matrices or sample logs.

Best,
Samantha Park
Head of Trust & Safety | LumenPay

Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation — technical timeline and matrix

Hi Samantha / team —

Thanks — I put together the retention matrix (attached) and a concise timeline below. High level:

- Live deletion: When LumenPay triggers a legal erase via the Redwood API or Console, the primary rowstore is deleted within seconds to a minute (depending on active requests). This generates a tombstone marker at the application layer + a deletion event in the audit stream.

- Short-term KV cache and backups: We maintain in-memory KV caches which are also invalidated on delete. Continuous backup snapshots (block-level) are created every 6 hours by default for Dedicated customers; snapshots are incremental. Snapshots respect retention policy but snapshots created prior to the delete will contain the data until they expire.

- Tombstone lifecycle: After deletion, a tombstone is retained for the configured tombstone TTL (default 7 days for Dedicated; configurable down to 1 day with contractual agreement). During this TTL the tombstone prevents resurrection during replication. After TTL expires, the record is eligible for expunge.

- Expunge / background sweep: Expunge runs as a background process; typical expunge windows are aligned to snapshot pruning cycles. In most US regions the complete expunge from all hot/cold replicas and replicated snapshots occurs within 7–14 days. Offsite/archival copies (if you opt into offsite archival) can have additional retention — those are controlled separately and we recommend 0–30 day archival hold for payments teams.

- Immutable media: We do not write production data to long-lived tape in our hosted offering. Offsite archive is object storage with immutability options; if you enable immutable-write archival the minimum retention is specified in the archival config (this would be a contract opt-in).

Audit evidence we can provide:
- Snapshot manifest listing snapshot ids and timestamps (sample attached).
- Audit-log slice showing the delete event and tombstone id (attached file).
- Expunge job run records (timestamp + job id) showing when sweep removed object versions.

Edge cases / notes:
- Cross-region replication: If you have geo-replicated replicas, deletion propagation follows event-order; replicas apply tombstones within seconds but physical expunge runs on each region's retention schedule. Expect up to an additional 24–48 hour variance per region if replication is across continents.
- Legal hold: If a legal hold is placed, our standard expunge is suspended and we provide hold status + proof of suspension.

I've attached snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx and audit-log-sample.txt to this thread. Let me know if you'd like a simplified one-page timeline for your compliance deck.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: snapshot-retention-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), audit-log-sample.txt (text)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@lumenpay.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation — compliance evidence

Hi Samantha —

Following Ben's technical summary, a couple of compliance items to highlight for your review: 

1) Evidence bundle we can provide programmatically (ideal for audits):
   - Delete event audit log (JSON or CSV slice) with event id, issuer, target id, and nonce.
   - Snapshot manifest (CSV) that shows pre-delete snapshot ids and expiration timestamps.
   - Expunge job record (signed) with job id and SHA256 digest of removed object versions.

2) Timeline example for a typical US-only account (no archival enabled, default settings):
   - T0: Delete request via API/console — delete event emitted and tombstone applied (seconds).
   - T0 + 6h: Next incremental snapshot may still contain data (if snapshot captured before T0).
   - T0 + 7 days: Tombstone TTL expires (default).
   - T0 + 7–14 days: Background expunge removes object versions from all replicas and prunes snapshots that are eligible.
   - Evidence package available within 24h after expunge job completes.

3) Contractal controls we usually add for payments customers:
   - Reduce tombstone TTL to 1–3 days (requires SLA/operational change).
   - Disable offsite archival for a subset of datasets to ensure no long-lived copies.
   - Add a written attestation clause and a monthly expunge report delivery (CSV/Drive link).

If you'd like, I can prepare a one-page compliance statement with exact fields LumenPay should present to auditors and a sample audit bundle (signed).

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Park <samantha.park@lumenpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Wilson <alex.wilson@lumenpay.com>, security@lumenpay.com
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup retention & deletion propagation — compliance evidence

Thank you all — this is exactly what we need. A few quick next steps from our side: 

- We'll review Ben's matrix and the audit log sample internally and confirm whether we need tombstone TTL reduced or archival disabled.
- Can you prepare the one-page compliance statement and the sample evidence bundle (signed) by next Wednesday? Our compliance review is Thursday morning.
- If there are any contract language tweaks (attestation clause / monthly expunge report), please flag them and we can loop procurement.

Let's also schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the timeline and any opt-ins. Proposed times: Mon 10:00–11:00 PT or Mon 15:00–15:30 PT.

Best,
Samantha
